name: Cain
summary: Cain brought of the fruit of the ground and Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering, and not unto Cain's, and Cain was very wroth. He was called to repent, and warned that if he did not, sin lay at the door. He talked with Abel in the field and slew him, then answered God with a lie and a taunt.
offense: When God did not regard Cain's offering, Cain became very wroth and his countenance fell. Before the murder, God addressed him: if he did well, he would be accepted; if not, sin lay at the door (Genesis 4:3-7). The warning made room for repentance. Rejection of the offering did not require him to become a murderer. Cain answered his brother's righteousness with violence. In the field he rose against Abel and slew him, then denied knowledge of him and asked whether he was his brother's keeper (Genesis 4:8-9). John names the motive plainly: Cain was of that wicked one, and slew his brother because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous (1 John 3:12). He would destroy the man whose conduct exposed his own instead of doing the good set before him. The warning of sin at the door and Peter's warning of the devouring adversary belong together (Genesis 4:7; 1 Peter 5:8). Anger nourished rather than corrected becomes an opening for further evil. The offering, the fallen countenance, the killing, and the lie show a course of refusal, not an unavoidable act forced upon him by God's rebuke.
judgment: Abel's blood cried from the ground. The earth that received it would no longer yield its strength to Cain, and he was made a fugitive and a vagabond (Genesis 4:10-12). His work as a tiller was struck by the sentence. He could not bury the deed and continue as though the ground held no witness against him.

entries.commentary: Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground.

The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry.

The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at [Genesis 3:21](/bible/genesis/3#v21). If Cain would not repent, sin lay at the door; he would become subject to Satan and Satan would rule over him.
When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.
Cain was cursed from the earth and made a fugitive and a vagabond, the same low estate spoken of the serpent in chapter 3.

Every one that findeth me shall slay me is proof in the pudding, like we brought out in [Genesis 1](/bible/genesis/1), that there were more people on the earth than Adam's household. The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him.

Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam. Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled. The lands in those days were named after men, which is why the land was called Nod. Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

This is the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it. In the beginning it was one wife. When you read about the sons of God in [Genesis 5](/bible/genesis/5) you do not read about them taking multiple wives; only the sons of the wicked.
An instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: these men started making weapons. This is the first you read about weapons being created.

Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time.

Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?
If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;
When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
